17import logging 

18 

19import torch 

20 

21logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

22 

23 

24def adjoint(self: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor: 

25 """Return the conjugate transpose view of ``self``. 

26 

27 Mirrors ``aten::adjoint(Tensor(a) self) -> Tensor(a)``: a zero-copy 

28 aliasing view with ``out[..., j, i] = conj(self[..., i, j])``. The 

29 returned tensor shares the input's storage with the last two strides 

30 swapped and, for complex inputs, carries the lazy conjugate bit, so no 

31 kernel is launched and no element data is touched (metadata-only op, 

32 no ceremonial Triton kernel). 

33 

34 - Real dtypes: ``conj`` is the identity, so the adjoint view is the 

35 plain transpose view ``self.mT``. 

36 - Complex dtypes: the view additionally carries the lazy conjugate bit 

37 (``self.mH``), which composes correctly with inputs that already hold 

38 a conjugate bit (the bits cancel, matching native ATen). 

39 - 0-D tensors: transpose is undefined, the op degrades to the conj view 

40 ``self.mH`` (a no-op conjugation for real 0-D inputs), like ATen. 

41 

42 ``mT``/``mH`` dispatch to the distinct ``aten::mT``/``aten::mH`` 

43 operators (verified: registering only ``adjoint`` cannot re-enter this 

44 implementation), and for 1-D inputs they raise the same 

45 "matrices or batches of matrices" ``RuntimeError`` as native ``adjoint``. 

46 """ 

47 logger.debug("GEMS ADJOINT") 

48 if self.ndim == 0: 

49 # 0-D: native adjoint() emits a deprecation warning and degrades to 

50 # conj(). Reproduce the warning text natively (delegating to self.mH 

51 # would expose the Tensor.mH deprecation warning instead). 

52 import warnings as _warnings 

53 

54 _warnings.warn( 

55 "adjoint() is deprecated on 0-D tensors. Consider using x.conj().", 

56 UserWarning, 

57 stacklevel=2, 

58 ) 

59 return self.conj() 

60 if self.ndim < 2: 

61 # 1-D real tensor: native adjoint() raises with its own message 

62 # naming adjoint(), not mT. Reproduce it before delegating. 

63 raise RuntimeError( 

64 f"tensor.adjoint() is only supported on matrices or batches of " 

65 f"matrices. Got {self.ndim}-D tensor." 

66 ) 

67 if self.dtype.is_complex: 

68 return self.mH 

69 return self.mT
